children.translated_text: The five principal jewels and the group of four secondary jewels
are written down here after distinguishing them, according to their value and according to their qualities.

children.text: vajraṃ ca mauktikaṃ caiva māṇikyaṃ nīlam eva ca
children.translated_text: Diamond, pearl, ruby, and sapphire,
and the emerald jewel: these are the great jewels in five divisions.
I shall tell the four secondary jewels; listen to that:

children.text: gomedaṃ puṣyarāgaṃ ca vaiḍūryaṃ ca pravālakam ||
children.translated_text: hessonite, yellow sapphire, cat's-eye, and coral.

children.text: vajraṃ ca mauktikaṃ śvetaṃ māṇikyaṃ lohitaṃ viduḥ
children.translated_text: They know diamond and pearl to be white, and ruby to be red;

children.text: nīlaṃ nīlaṃ samākhyātaṃ marakataṃ haritaṃ hitam ||
children.translated_text: sapphire is called blue, and emerald is beneficially green.

children.text: śvetaṃ pītaṃ ca gomedaṃ puṣyarāgaṃ ca piñjaram
children.translated_text: Hessonite is white and yellow, and yellow sapphire is tawny;
coral is said to be red, and cat's-eye is greenish-white.

children.text: kośale ca kaliṅge ca magadhe ca himālaye
children.translated_text: In <s>Kośala</s>, in <s>Kaliṅga</s>, in <s>Magadha</s>, in the <s>Himālaya</s>,
in <s>Pauṇḍrākara</s>, and in <s>Saurāṣṭra</s> are the places where diamond is produced.

children.text: ratnānām uttamaṃ vajraṃ yo bibharti narottamaḥ
children.translated_text: A diamond is the best of jewels; the best of men who wears it

children.text: uttamaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ yathā śakras tathaiva saḥ ||
children.translated_text: is himself like <s>Śakra</s>, the best of all beings.

children.text: abhedyaṃ ca tathādāhyam aśoṣyākledyam eva ca
children.translated_text: It is unbreakable, likewise unburnable, incapable of being dried or wetted;

children.text: yathaivātmā tathā vajraṃ tasmān maulyaṃ samarpayet ||
children.translated_text: as the self is, so is the diamond; therefore one should assign its value.
Seven defects and qualities have been declared by experts in jewels;
for superior, inferior, and middling stones, the value is twelvefold.

children.text: malaṃ bindur yavo rekhā veṣagyam kākapādavat
children.translated_text: Impurity, a spot, a barley-grain mark, a line, crookedness, and crow-foot-like marking:
these five defects are to be rejected, for they give fruits of many kinds of suffering.

children.text: tuṅgaṃ vajraṃ praśaṃsanti ṣaṭkoṇaṃ laghu bhāskaram
children.translated_text: They praise a high diamond, six-cornered, light, and shining,
with very sharp edges, eight-angled, and smooth with rays on every side.
Untimely death, snakes, fire, enemies, and fears from diseases

children.text: dūrāt tasya praṇaśyanti vajraṃ yasya gṛhe bhavet ||
children.translated_text: perish from afar for the one in whose house there is a diamond.
For a faultless stone of the measure of a barley-grain, gathered with brilliance on every side,

children.text: pañcāśad bhavati maulyaṃ ratnaśāstre hy udāhṛtam ||
children.translated_text: the value is fifty, as stated in the science of jewels.

children.text: piṇḍato dviguṇasthaulyaṃ taulyaṃ caiva yadā bhavet
children.translated_text: When in mass it has twice the thickness and the same weight,

children.text: caturguṇaṃ bhaven mūlyaṃ triguṇe tv aṣṭamaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: the price should become fourfold; when it is threefold, it is as though eightfold.

children.text: śveto raktas tathā pītaḥ kṛṣṇaś ca kuliśo bhavet
children.translated_text: The thunderbolt-stone may be white, red, yellow, or black;
the distinction of class is imagined in the order beginning with the Brahmin.

children.text: uttamaṃ brāhmaṇe maulyaṃ madhyamaṃ kṣatriye tathā
children.translated_text: The best value belongs to the Brahmin class, the middling likewise to the Kṣatriya;
the ordinary value is in the Vaiśya class, and the lowest in birth as a Śūdra.

children.text: yan maulyaṃ brāhmaṇe proktam pādonaṃ kṣatriye smṛtam
children.translated_text: The value stated for the Brahmin is remembered as less by a quarter for the Kṣatriya;
by this very sequence it decreases in due order.

children.text: vajram ca trividhaṃ proktaṃ naro narī napuṃsakam
children.translated_text: Diamond is said to be of three kinds: male, female, and neuter.
Eight-angled and eight-faceted, six-cornered, and shining,
like a cloud, a rainbow, or water-bearing, it is called a male diamond.

children.text: tad eva cet pītākāraṃ strīvajraṃ vartulāya ca ||
children.translated_text: If that same stone has a yellow form and is round, it is a female diamond.
Round, with blunt corners and angles, and somewhat broad, it is neuter.
Female, male, and neuter diamonds should be matched with women, men, and neuters.

children.text: tyajyaṃ syān naiva phaladaṃ puṃvajreṇa vinā kvacit
children.translated_text: Otherwise it should be rejected; it is nowhere fruitful without a male diamond.
It gives the respective fruits of the Brahmin, Kṣatriya, Vaiśya, and Śūdra classes.

children.text: kṛtrimatvaṃ yathā vajre kathyate sūribhiḥ kvacit
children.translated_text: The artificial nature of a diamond is sometimes described by wise men as follows.

children.text: kṣārāmlair lepayed vajraṃ gharme ca pariśodhayet
children.translated_text: One should smear the diamond with alkalis and acids and purify it in heat.
An artificial one undergoes discoloration, while a natural one shines exceedingly.
Color, mass, and heaviness increase according to the progression of tiny increments;
everywhere the value increases according to the nature of qualities and defects.
This stone called <s>Māhendra</s> should be worn; it gives abundance of wealth and grain.
It gives sons, is purifying and venerable, destroys enemies, and gives fearlessness in battle.

children.text: gurviṇībhir na dhartavyo yuvatībhir ayam maṇiḥ
children.translated_text: This jewel should not be worn by pregnant women or by young women,
for from contact with diamond in the belly there will be miscarriage.
Those born from cloud, elephant, fish, snake, bamboo, conch, and boar,
and those arisen from oyster-shell: these should be known as the eight kinds of pearl.
In cloud-born pearls there is a pure form; in elephant-born ones, a rosy splendor;

children.text: hariśvetaṃ tathā vaṃśe pītaśvetaṃ ca śūkare ||
children.translated_text: in bamboo-born pearls there is yellowish-white color, and in boar-born pearls yellow-white.
Those arisen from conch and oyster-shell are white; such is the sequence of pearl-gems.

children.text: rāgas trāsaś ca binduś ca rekhā ca jalagarbhatā
children.translated_text: Coloring, trembling, a spot, a line, and watery interior:

children.text: sarvaratneṣv amī pañca doṣāḥ sādhāraṇā matāḥ
children.translated_text: these five are considered common defects in all jewels.

children.text: kṣetratoyabhavā doṣā ratneṣu na laganti te ||
children.translated_text: Defects born of the field or water do not attach to jewels.

children.text: hari śvetaṃ laghu snigdhaṃ raśmivan nirmalaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: Greenish-white, light, unctuous, radiant, stainless, large,

children.text: khyātam toyaprabhaṃ vṛttaṃ mauktikaṃ navadhā śubham ||
children.translated_text: renowned, water-bright, and round: a pearl with these nine traits is auspicious.
A pearl that is fine-bodied, clear-dark, coppery in appearance, like salt,

children.text: ardhaṃ ca vikaṭam granthikaṃ mauktikaṃ tyajet ||
children.translated_text: half-formed, misshapen, or knotty should be rejected.
Whatever value is declared here for a white pearl-gem,
one quarter less should be made for the jewel called maṇi.
A jewel the size of a jujube fruit and equal in radiance to the rising sun
is said to be liktada; it gives the fruits of enjoyment and liberation.

children.text: sacchidraṃ karkaśaṃ kṣaudraṃ raktābhaṃ ca sabindukam
children.translated_text: A pearl with holes, rough, honey-colored, reddish, and spotted,

children.text: malinaṃ niṣprabhaṃ citraṃ bhagnam tu mauktikaṃ tyajet ||
children.translated_text: dirty, lusterless, variegated, or broken should be rejected.

children.text: svacchābhaṃ ca suvṛttaṃ ca guru snigdhaṃ ca nirmalam
children.translated_text: Clear in appearance, perfectly round, heavy, unctuous, and stainless,
high and moon-like in splendor: such a pearl-gem is priceless.
The Brahmin should be white in color, and the Kṣatriya like the sun;
the Vaiśya should have a yellow tinge, and the Śūdra should have his own luster.
Royal fortune, sons, and happiness, preceded by elephants, horses, and towns,

children.text: prāpnoty eva sajātiḥ syād gṛhe nirdoṣaśaṅkhajam ||
children.translated_text: One obtains it indeed; it should be of the same kind, produced from a flawless conch in the house.

children.text: suvṛttaṃ suprabhaṃ śvetaṃ guñjāmātram anardhi ca
children.translated_text: Well-rounded, very bright, white, measuring a guñjā, and not defective,
and valued at twenty-five: so it is stated in the science of jewels.

children.text: yathā ca vardhate muktā tathā maulyaṃ ca vardhate
children.translated_text: As a pearl increases, so too its value increases;

children.text: kṣīyate ca yathā muktā tathā maulyaṃ hi hīyate ||
children.translated_text: and as a pearl diminishes, so indeed its value decreases.

children.text: guñjānāṃ catuḥṣaṣṭyā bhāreṇa ca mitaṃ ca tat
children.translated_text: That measure is reckoned by the weight of sixty-four guñjās.
An excellent pearl, O Tamru, is fit to be valued at a crore.

children.text: mauktike yadi saṃdehaḥ kṛtrime sahaje 'pi vā
children.translated_text: If there is doubt about a pearl, whether artificial or natural,
then an examination should be made there by experts in the science of jewels.
One should heat it by fire, or wrap it in a white cloth;
taking the pearl in the hand, one should rub it with rice husk.
The artificial one breaks apart, but the natural one shines exceedingly.
